question_text: What is the sum of the interior angles of any convex quadrilateral?
hint_modal: Recall the fundamental theorems and rules presented in the chapter.

solution_key.final_solution: A quadrilateral can be split into 2 non-overlapping triangles. Since each triangle has an angle sum of 180 degrees, the quadrilateral interior angle sum is 2 * 180 = 360 degrees.

question_text: In a parallelogram, adjacent angles are _____.
hint_modal: Recall the fundamental theorems and rules presented in the chapter.

solution_key.final_solution: Because opposite sides are parallel, adjacent interior angles are consecutive interior angles between parallel lines, making them supplementary.

question_text: True or False: Every quadrilateral whose diagonals are perpendicular to each other is a rhombus.
hint_modal: Recall the fundamental theorems and rules presented in the chapter.

solution_key.final_solution: False. A kite also has perpendicular diagonals, but its diagonals do not bisect each other and its 4 sides are not all equal.

question_text: Two adjacent angles of a parallelogram are in the ratio 2:3. Find the measure of all four interior angles.
hint_modal: Recall the fundamental theorems and rules presented in the chapter.

solution_key.final_solution: Adjacent angles add to 180 degrees: 2x + 3x = 180 -> 5x = 180 -> x = 36. Angles are 2(36) = 72° and 3(36) = 108°. Opposite angles are equal, so the four angles are 72°, 108°, 72°, 108°.

question_text: Construct a diagonal matrix comparison: In which quadrilateral(s) are diagonals both EQUAL in length AND bisect each other at RIGHT ANGLES?
hint_modal: Recall the fundamental theorems and rules presented in the chapter.

solution_key.final_solution: Rectangles have equal diagonals that bisect each other (not at 90°). Rhombuses have diagonals bisecting at 90° (not equal length). Squares satisfy both conditions simultaneously.

question_text: Prove using triangle congruence (ASA/CPCTC) that opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal.
hint_modal: Recall the fundamental theorems and rules presented in the chapter.
correct_answer: In parallelogram ABCD, draw diagonal AC. AB || CD => Angle CAB = ACD. AD || BC => Angle CAD = ACB. AC is common. Triangle ABC congruent to CDA by ASA. Thus AB = CD and BC = DA by CPCTC.

solution_key.final_solution: By drawing diagonal AC, alternate interior angles are equal. Common side AC creates ASA triangle congruence, proving opposite sides equal by CPCTC.

question_text: A wooden window frame UVWX is constructed by joining the midpoints of the four sides of a square wall section CASE. Prove that UVWX is also a square.
hint_modal: Recall the fundamental theorems and rules presented in the chapter.
correct_answer: Joining side midpoints creates 4 congruent isosceles right triangles at corners. Hypotenuses UV=VW=WX=XU. Corner angles = 180 - 45 - 45 = 90 degrees, proving UVWX is a square.

solution_key.final_solution: Each corner triangle has leg lengths equal to half the square side. Hypotenuses are equal by Pythagoras theorem, and corner angles evaluate to 90°, fulfilling square criteria.
